subject: psych
source: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology (0266) syllabus for examination in 2027, 2028 and 2029 — Cambridge International; Year 10 covers Paper 1 content (topics 1–3: memory and forgetting, sleep and dreams, prosocial behaviour) with the experimental research method (7.1, 7.5–7.9)

weeks.topic: Experimental method: aims, hypotheses, independent and dependent variables
objectives: Write aims and directional and non-directional hypotheses
Identify and operationalise the IV and DV

weeks.topic: Experimental designs: independent measures, repeated measures and matched pairs
objectives: Compare the three experimental designs
Explain order effects and counterbalancing

weeks.topic: Laboratory, field and natural experiments; controlling variables
objectives: Compare types of experiment
Identify extraneous and confounding variables and how to control them

weeks.topic: Memory and forgetting: key concepts
objectives: Define encoding, storage and retrieval
Distinguish short-term and long-term memory by capacity, duration and encoding

weeks.topic: Craik and Lockhart's levels of processing model
objectives: Describe structural, phonetic and semantic processing
Evaluate the levels of processing model

weeks.topic: Core study: Craik and Tulving (1975) — levels of processing (experiment 2)
objectives: Describe the aim, procedure, results and conclusions
Evaluate the study's validity and reliability

weeks.topic: Atkinson and Shiffrin's multistore model of memory
objectives: Describe sensory, short-term and long-term stores
Explain rehearsal and transfer
Evaluate the model

weeks.topic: Core study: Murdock (1962) — the serial position effect
objectives: Describe the procedure and findings
Explain primacy and recency effects using the multistore model

weeks.topic: Motivated forgetting: repression
objectives: Explain motivated forgetting and repression
Evaluate the evidence for repressed memories

weeks.topic: The role of the brain in memory and forgetting: the hippocampus
objectives: Describe the role of the hippocampus in memory
Explain anterograde and retrograde amnesia

weeks.topic: Core study: Milner et al. (1968) — HM and amnesia
objectives: Describe the case of HM and findings
Evaluate case study evidence for memory models

weeks.topic: Sampling: target populations, random, opportunity and volunteer sampling
objectives: Define target population and sample
Compare sampling techniques and generalisability

weeks.topic: Validity and reliability
objectives: Define internal, external and ecological validity
Explain test-retest and inter-rater reliability

weeks.topic: Ethical guidelines
objectives: Explain informed consent, deception, right to withdraw, protection and confidentiality
Apply ethics to research scenarios

weeks.topic: Review: memory and forgetting and experimental research methods
objectives: Revise theories, core studies and key concepts
Practise Section A and Section D style questions

weeks.topic: Sleep and dreams: key concepts
objectives: Describe sleep stages, REM and NREM sleep
Explain circadian rhythms and the sleep cycle

weeks.topic: Restoration theory of sleep
objectives: Explain how sleep restores body and brain
Evaluate the theory using evidence

weeks.topic: Core study: Robinson et al. (2018) — sleep restriction
objectives: Describe the aim, procedure and findings
Evaluate the study's methodology

weeks.topic: Hobson and McCarley's activation-synthesis theory of dreaming
objectives: Explain random neural activation in REM sleep
Evaluate the biological explanation of dreams

weeks.topic: Core study: Williams et al. (1992) — bizarreness of dream content
objectives: Describe the procedure and findings
Link findings to activation-synthesis theory

weeks.topic: Psychodynamic theory of dreaming: Freud
objectives: Explain manifest and latent content and wish fulfilment
Describe dream work processes
Evaluate the theory

weeks.topic: Core study: Iorio et al. (2020) — dreams and trauma
objectives: Describe the aim, procedure and findings
Evaluate the study's design and ethics

weeks.topic: Role of the researcher, materials and procedure
objectives: Explain researcher effects and demand characteristics
Write standardised procedures and instructions

weeks.topic: Dealing with data: quantitative and qualitative data; central tendency
objectives: Distinguish quantitative and qualitative data
Calculate mean, median and mode

weeks.topic: Dealing with data: graphs, range and percentages
objectives: Draw bar charts and histograms
Calculate range and percentages
Interpret results tables

weeks.topic: Prosocial behaviour: key concepts
objectives: Define prosocial behaviour, altruism and helping
Explain the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: memory and forgetting, sleep and dreams and the experimental method
objectives: Complete a timed Paper 1 style exam
Apply research methods to novel scenarios

weeks.topic: Biological explanation of prosocial behaviour
objectives: Explain kin selection and genetic influences on helping
Evaluate the biological approach

weeks.topic: Core study: Rushton (2004) — heritability of social responsibility
objectives: Describe the twin study method and findings
Evaluate the nature–nurture conclusions

weeks.topic: Social identity theory of prosocial behaviour
objectives: Explain in-groups, out-groups and social categorisation
Apply the theory to helping behaviour

weeks.topic: Core study: Levine et al. (2005) — helping behaviour (study 1)
objectives: Describe the procedure using football fans and findings
Evaluate the field experiment

weeks.topic: Bandura's social learning theory of prosocial behaviour
objectives: Explain observation, imitation, modelling and vicarious reinforcement
Apply SLT to prosocial behaviour

weeks.topic: Core study: Prot et al. (2014) — prosocial media (study 1)
objectives: Describe the cross-cultural survey and findings
Evaluate correlational evidence

weeks.topic: Designing and evaluating your own experiment (Paper 1 Section D)
objectives: Plan an experiment with hypothesis, design, sample and procedure
Evaluate your plan for validity, reliability and ethics

weeks.topic: Extended response skills: the 8-mark question
objectives: Structure answers combining description, application and evaluation
Use core study evidence effectively

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: full Paper 1 (memory, sleep, prosocial behaviour, experiments)
objectives: Complete a full Paper 1 under exam conditions
Review performance in each section

weeks.topic: Review: prosocial behaviour and dealing with data
objectives: Correct errors from end-of-year exams
Consolidate core studies before Year 11
